So on this event the accept/reject boundary is set by cluster connectivity, not by the dist/angle gate at all. It is a single 38.6 cm segment, chord 35.1 cm, transverse RMS 0.54 cm over its 65 skeleton points (2*RMS/L = 0.03) -- dead straight and ~1 cm wide, with no lateral development anywhere along it in the az-055 or az+085 shower frames. Reading (b), which I could NOT exclude and which is why this is unclear: the vertex sits inside a large, lattice-textured point cloud, and if that cloud is real charge then 22004 could be the skeleton core of a genuine shower whose lateral charge simply has no segments drawn through it -- in which case the object is an EM shower and the event is badly under-clustered. What stopped me calling the cloud missing shower charge: it is a THIN SHEET, not a 3-D blob -- in shw22004-az+085-el+20 the whole cloud collapses to a band ~4.5 cm across while in az-055 it is 50+ cm wide, and its texture is a regular diagonal hatch. Vertex judged off the vtxz-* close-in sweep at 60 cm half-span (correction 20; r95 = 355.3 cm and event_half_span_cm is saturated at 400.0 -- correction 19 -- so the vtx-* sweep at 400 cm is useless here): the star sits at the downstream end of the 404.8 cm muon with 22001 and 22003 also on it, which is a normal numu CC vertex; not vertex-bad.
